page: Microsoft Azure D4s_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture, managed via Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz with two threads per core. System memory totals 16.0 GB, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The CPU configuration features 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large shared 260 MB L3 cache. It incorporates instruction extensions including AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, and SHA-NI, while lacking integrated GPUs and bundled local ephemeral storage.

Benchmark testing demonstrates average performance in single-threaded tasks alongside lower throughput in sustained multi-core operations. Single-core evaluations show a stress-ng metric of 1896.88 and a Geekbench score of 1640.0, both falling within the median cloud performance range. Cryptographic and compression throughput also perform solidly at the baseline, with single-threaded gzip reaching 28.44 GB/sec and PassMark encryption scoring 3644.51. However, multi-core benchmarks such as stress-ng multi-core (3867.37), Geekbench multi-core (3524.0), and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (19.72 GB/sec) place in the bottom 25% or lower, indicating constraints inherent to a 2-core, 4-thread execution footprint.

Memory subsystem testing reveals uncached read bandwidth of 29.75 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 25.9 GB/sec for large 256 MB blocks, accompanied by a PassMark memory score of 2000.05. Small-block cached reads reach 208.51 GB/sec. Application-oriented tests display balanced output for static web serving at 6.44 GB/sec and small-model LLM text generation at 109.01 tokens/sec. Conversely, high-concurrency tasks such as PassMark database operations (2036.16) and Redis SET operations (3.98 million operations/sec) reflect weaker relative throughput.

The absence of local disks necessitates reliance on remote Premium Storage attached via network storage protocols. Microsoft Azure D4s_v5 delivers cost-efficient utility for standard enterprise workloads that do not saturate multi-threaded capacity, including web application hosting, mid-scale development environments, microservices, and general compute tasks with moderate I/O demands.
description: Microsoft Azure D4s_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Managed by Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, alongside 16.0 GB of memory. It features 260 MB of L3 cache and supports AVX-512 vector extensions, but omits local storage and dedicated GPUs. Benchmarks demonstrate solid average results in single-threaded compute, static web serving (6.44 GB/sec), and basic cryptographic workloads. However, multi-threaded scaling remains in lower performance tiers due to the 2-core topology. The instance is suitable for web serving, microservices, and standard enterprise applications using network-attached block storage.
